title: Our Streets Collective official site

data.notes: Current first-party Pittsburgh site self-describes a mutual-aid collective working with poor and unhoused neighbors against capitalist exploitation. Current services include survival material, food, harm reduction, jail support and community connection. Public contacts include support@ourstreetscollective.com, (412) 636-4148, (412) 449-9031, Venmo @OurStreets1312, Patreon OurStreetsCollective, and an official-site Instagram link resolving to @our_streets_collective.

title: Our Streets Collective 2026 public interview

title: Pittsburgh Prison Book Project official site

data.notes: Current first-party site describes PPBP as an all-volunteer Pittsburgh organization sending books to incarcerated people across Pennsylvania, serving about 200 people and mailing about 500 items monthly. It says PPBP is a project of Let's Get Free and The Big Idea Book Store; after Thomas Merton Center sunset in 2025, Let's Get Free became fiscal sponsor. Current contact page lists pghprisonbookproject@gmail.com, Facebook PittsburghPrisonBookProject, and X/Twitter @PGHPBP.

title: Area-code-hunt shard B pass — NPAs 406, 409, 412

data.research_question: Which public organizations relevant to the anarchist-violence organization-enumeration corpus are discoverable from the next unresolved authoritative shard-B U.S. geographic NPAs 406, 409 and 412?
data.method: Bounded area-code organization enumeration using authoritative NANPA admission before deterministic NPA mod 3 sharding; literal anarchist, anarchist collective, Anarchist Black Cross, Food Not Bombs and mutual-aid queries; locality-derived searches; current first-party organization pages; public social and resource hubs; public Reddit discovery without official APIs; historical anarchist/Food Not Bombs directories only as discovery seeds; and repository exact-name search before canonical-ID creation.
classification_rules: Do not infer individual political affiliation from organization proximity or event participation.
Do not label an organization anarchist absent explicit organization-level evidence.
Historical directories and old social endpoints are discovery seeds until current status is corroborated.
Do not merge identities from name or handle similarity alone.
Completed NPAs are not repeated without materially new evidence.
A zero-hit code remains a zero-hit control instead of being padded with generic charities or ideologically unrelated organizations.

findings.notes: Missoula Food Not Bombs has current 2026 institutional partnership evidence and recent recurring meal-service discovery; a current first-party social hub remains unresolved.

Beaumont, Galveston, Port Arthur and nearby locality-derived/literal searches did not produce a sufficiently evidence-backed anarchist, ABC/ABCF, Food Not Bombs or mutual-aid organization for materialization. Environmental-justice and civic groups found in the search were not padded into this corpus absent the requested organizational evidence.

Pittsburgh produced a current self-described anarchist collective (The Big Idea), current abolitionist/anti-capitalist mutual aid (Our Streets Collective), current/recent Steel City Food Not Bombs activity, and Pittsburgh Prison Book Project as a current evidence-backed outward project edge from The Big Idea.

Resolve Steel City Food Not Bombs' currently organization-owned Instagram and Facebook endpoints from a first-party hub; current public resource directories support the handles but do not prove ownership as strongly as a first-party page.
Follow Pittsburgh Prison Book Project's current Let's Get Free fiscal-sponsorship edge in a later bounded outward pass without conflating the two organizations.
Follow The Big Idea's current event/co-sponsor and local anarchist-space edges, re-verifying historical Northeast Anarchist Network/infoshop references against current sources.
Map Our Streets Collective's current National Union of the Homeless and recurring distribution relations using direct organization-level evidence.
Re-check Pittsburgh Black Rose/Rosa Negra and ABC/ABCF directory leads for current first-party evidence before materializing any historical identities.

gaps: Some social endpoints remain public-directory corroborated rather than first-party owned.
NPA 409 remains a deliberate zero-hit control after bounded current-status search.
Food Not Bombs family association is recorded without upgrading local chapters to self-described anarchist organizations absent explicit local evidence.
